modules.module_title: Operate the Electro-Mechanical System in a Small Hydro Plant

pcs.pc_description: Explain basic concepts of electricity and prevalent energy-efficient devices typically used in a small hydro plant.
Identify the various types of turbines, switchyards and drive systems, their components (such as runner, casing nozzle/guide vanes, belts and pulleys etc.) along with their usage.
Explain the functioning of governors, oil pumping unit (OPU) and hydroelectric generator (Induction and Synchronous).
Describe the operating and maintenance procedure of a heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC), automatic voltage regulator (AVR), power transformers and excitation systems.
Elaborate the use of compressors, compressed air system, cooling water system, unit control switchboard configurations and control circuitry configurations.
Illustrate how to work as per the layout of the workstation and the electrical and thermal equipment used at site
Explain the applications of unit auxiliary transformers, AC supply and distribution boards.

Elaborate the typical operation and functioning of LV switchgear (with respect to their ratings and testing procedures), illumination, battery chargers, DC distribution boards, inverters, UPS, DG sets and HVAC loads at SHP stations.
Describe typical motors used in pumps and electrical cranes.
Explain the use of power cables and communication channels and their typical earth faults (such as overheating) and defects along with their rectification.
Demonstrate the steps for drainage and dewatering of pumps.
Show how to use equipment handling devices such as crane, pulley block etc. along with their dismantling and assembling.
Employ standard operating techniques to maintain and inspect hydroelectric generators at site such as drying out and testing generators before commissioning.
Perform routine testing of the control system at site.
Demonstrate how to test various meters, instruments, devices, scanners, transducers, switchboards etc.
Show how to repair instrument, meters and other electrical devices.
Employ various approved procedures for waste management such as minimizing waste.
Demonstrate how to optimise utilization of material and water and applying common practices for conserving electricity and other resources.
Perform various factory and field tests on power transformers.
Demonstrate how to dry out and test unit auxiliary transformers at site.
Employ standard/prescribed techniques for installation, maintenance and testing of batteries at SHP stations.
Explain various faults and abnormalities in the system such as vibrations and unexpected noises.
Describe the causes of overheating and its prevention.
Elaborate usage and functioning of tapered locking sleeves and tapered adapter sleeves.
Differentiate between different types of bearings, their fittings and shaft alignment.
Discuss the application of protection systems for SHP stations.
Explain the importance/relevance of grounding for switchyard equipment.
Elaborate the application of isolators and their typical configurations for small hydro plants.
Describe the usage of different types of circuit Breakers .
Explain the usage of bus-bars and test bus equipment for maintenance of the system at site.
Demonstrate how to dismantle and assemble equipment.
Employ standard techniques to identify and rectify defects in the system.
Show how to diagnose fault conditions in equipment.
Perform steps to configure and maintain lightning protection for SHP station.
Demonstrate how to use load break switches, power fuses and circuit switchers to avoid breakdown of the system.
